title: Records as bytes
description:
Store score records in a fixed binary layout with `struct`: a little-endian unsigned 32-bit id, a name in 8 bytes (UTF-8, padded with zero bytes) and an unsigned 1-byte score.

- `pack_record(id, name, score) -> bytes` (13 bytes); a name longer than 8 bytes once encoded, or a score above 255, raises `ValueError`.
- `unpack_record(data) -> tuple` gives `(id, name, score)` back, with the zero padding removed.

```python
data = pack_record(1, "Ada", 91)
print(data.hex(" "))           # 01 00 00 00 41 64 61 00 00 00 00 00 5b
print(unpack_record(data))     # (1, 'Ada', 91)
```
hints: `struct.pack("<I8sB", id, name.encode("utf-8"), score)`: the `8s` field pads a short byte string with zeros for you (lesson 8.04).
Unpacking gives the 8 name bytes; `.rstrip(b"\0").decode("utf-8")` turns them back into text.
